texts: bad: 'a bright lantern' is an indefinite singular with an ordinary verb, which the translator has to read as one particular lantern — so the log entry is recorded as a one-off fact about a witness lantern instead of the world rule it states (compare sentences 3 and 4, whose bare-plural subjects did come out as rules). Write it as an explicit universal: 'On day 396 of Year 2, Coraline Ash wrote in her log that every bright lantern draws a crowd of nightmoths.' Two translator-side slips no rewrite touches: 'in her log' was filed as the writing's physical location rather than its medium, and 'day 396 of Year 2' has no defined reading because the day slot is a day-of-month.

bad: the same indefinite-singular problem — 'a crowd of nightmoths' becomes one particular crowd, so the entry records an episode rather than the general law it states. Make the quantification explicit: 'Coraline Ash wrote in her log that every crowd of nightmoths brings sky-cats down from the cliff-spires.' ('in her log' is filed as a physical location here too — same translator-side slip.)

bad: 'hunting sky-cats' is a prenominal participle that carries its own event, and the translator turned it into a hunt event sitting inside the rule's condition — a condition naming an event nothing ever asserts, so the rule can never fire (the fireability check flags exactly this). Give the condition its own finite clause with an explicit subject: 'Coraline Ash wrote in her log that when sky-cats hunt, they molt feathers.'

mixed: the sealed rule is right and fireable — 'ground feathers' rides as a plain adjective in the condition and the make-it-safe result comes out in the licensed shape. The only flaw is the recurring 'in her log' being filed as the writing's location rather than its medium, which is a translator-side slot choice rather than anything your wording caused; no rewrite needed here.

mixed: the roles are right (Coraline the reader, the note read, Pell the addressee), but 'at breakfast' is parked in the time slot, which admits only calendar expressions and parts of the day — a meal is neither — and 'the note' is minted as a brand-new object with no link back to what she wrote in her log. 'Coraline Ash read her log to Pell during breakfast.' fixes both: 'during' gets a licensed relation to a reified breakfast, and 'her log' reuses the same log symbol the four entries were written in.
